name: first alias flips from T1 to T2 at 3 bits
note: The SFT model always calls the first selected column's table T1 and then orders FROM to match. The 3-bit model writes T2 after 'SELECT T' and still orders FROM the same way, so the column is on the wrong alias. One token decision, made the same way every time: a candidate for the single obstacle the protocol asks about. name: the T2 flip is a rounding error in two weights of the embedding table

evidence.the stream at coordinate 425 (after the: -45.4, sd 2.1 over questions; a typical coordinate is about 1
evidence.row '1' (token 16), coordinate 425: full precision 0.04053, stored at level 0.05298 (code 6); the level below is 0.02649; step 0.02649
evidence.row '2' (token 17), coordinate 425: full precision 0.03320, stored at level 0.02246 (code 5); the level above is 0.04492; step 0.02246

note: The 3-bit model's own computation still prefers T1: its final stream read through the full-precision rows gives +0.79. The flip comes from the output rows of the tied embedding for the tokens '1' and '2'. The decision's margin is thin at full precision (0.5, the training data has T1 first about 60% of the time), and one coordinate of the stream is about 45 times a typical one. On that coordinate both weights sat within 3% of a step from the midpoint between two levels and were rounded in opposite directions, which moves the logit difference by -1.05. The other 2,047 coordinates add -0.76, about what unbiased rounding noise gives (random-walk size 1.2).

name: alias_reround
reason: Re-round the two near-tied weights to their other neighbouring level. Each stays a rounding of its full-precision value to an adjacent level (error 0.53 and 0.52 of a step in place of 0.47 and 0.48). This turns coordinate 425's share of the read-out error from -1.05 into +1.18, so the total goes from -1.81 to +0.41 and the margin for T1 from -1.03 to +1.20 on the traced questions (computed from the stored streams, no new pass). Re-rounding only one of the two leaves a margin near 0.2, too thin to hold on every question.

prediction.behaviour: answers that use aliases start 'SELECT T1.' again; the missing-column errors where the column is on another alias of the same query (118 of 222) mostly go away; accuracy on join questions rises from 10 of 205. Single-table questions should not move.

name: the 3-bit model has other systematic habits
the same read-out error flips other thin decisions
note: The alias flip came from rounding error in two output rows on a coordinate where the stream is huge. Every token's output row has such an error, so every logit carries a fixed offset of up to about a logit. If that is what makes the 3-bit model stop early, add DISTINCT and over-join, then at the first token where it leaves the full-precision answer, reading its own stream through the full-precision output rows should give the full-precision token back. Test: the 3-bit model reads the full-precision model's answers on 256 practice questions (256 sequences); the stored streams are then read through both sets of rows offline.

name: alias_reround

target.what: the fused SFT model at MLX 3-bit
target.why_this_precision: the single obstacle found exists only at 3 bits: the first alias is T1 in 191 of 192 aliased answers at full precision, 223 of 224 at 4 bits and 2 of 234 at 3 bits

reason: At 3 bits the model writes T2 as the first alias and then orders its tables as if it had written T1, so the selected column is on the wrong alias. Its own computation still prefers T1 (+0.79 logits when its final stream is read through the full-precision output rows). The flip comes from the output rows for the tokens '1' and '2' in the tied embedding table: on coordinate 425, where the final stream is about 45 times a typical coordinate, both weights sat within 3% of a step from the midpoint between two levels and were rounded in opposite directions (-1.05 of the -1.81 logit read-out error). The edit moves each to its other neighbouring level, so each is still its full-precision value rounded to an adjacent level of the same grid.

Seeds 1 to 5. Same rows, same form, same size (2 codes).

The report says how far it matches the stored run that gave 0.3733. Rule: docs/weight_edit/PROTOCOL.md, 'The test, run once', as coded in src/shrinkwrap/weight_edit/verdict.py.

How much accuracy that buys is not known: on practice most repaired answers were still wrong for other reasons. The controls should score within a few answers of the unedited model.
